claims.explanation: Mocetinostat is a class I HDAC inhibitor whose selectivity is best explained by dependence on class I HDAC activity and an intact, HDAC-repressible epigenetic/immune program rather than by a single lineage. Sensitive lines are enriched for TP53 mutation together with activating PI3K/AKT-pathway and receptor-tyrosine-kinase lesions (PIK3CA, EGFR, ERBB2/ERBB3, MET, BRAF), whereas resistant lines are enriched for NF2 loss, KRAS-only pancreatic contexts, and EP300/CREBBP or SWI/SNF (SMARCA4/ARID1A) alterations that may bypass HDAC dependence. High baseline expression of class I HDACs and of HDAC-repressed immune/antigen-presentation genes (HLA, PD-L1) is predicted to further sensitize lines.

features.basis: TP53 mutation is near-universal in selectively killed lines and absent in several resistant lines
Activating PI3K lesions enriched in sensitive lines (KYSE70, HCC1954, T47D, HGC27, 253J, BFTC909)
EGFR-mutant lines (KYSE70, NCIH1650) among most killed
ERBB2-mutant SW480 and ERBB3-mutant lung lines are sensitive
MET-mutant 8305C and HGC27 are among most killed
BRAF-mutant 8305C and WM793 are sensitive
NF2 loss enriched in least-affected lines (CAL62, S117, YD8, NCIH2052, mesothelioma)
EP300/CREBBP-mutant lines (NCIH1339, CAL62, LU99) are resistant, suggesting bypass of HDAC dependence
CREBBP-mutant CAL62 is among least affected
SMARCA4-mutant lines (NCIH1703, NCIH1793, EKVX, NCIH1573) are predominantly resistant
ARID1A-mutant lines appear in both groups but enriched among resistant (NCIH1793, OVTOKO, SUIT2)
Mocetinostat targets class I HDACs; high HDAC1/2/3 expression predicts dependence
